solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: England cricketer's remarks? They can be cutting and lethal!

definitions.text: They can be cutting and lethal!

parts.note: Stuart Broad, the England fast bowler; with the possessive it reads as Broad's
remarks are things said, words

explanation.surface: A quip about a famous England bowler's sharp tongue, whose comments wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Stuart Broad was a long-serving England cricket fast bowler. Read 'Broad's words' as one run of letters and you have heavy swords.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-bladed swords are weapons made for slashing, hence cutting and deadly.

clue.text: Obscure group involved in attack

indicators.note: one piece being involved in another means it sits within it

parts.note: a bout is a fit or attack of illness
a lot is a group or set of items, as at auction

explanation.surface: A shadowy gang has taken part in an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to hide it from view, as by covering it with ink or cloud.

clue.text: Decree from Iran — do get troubled

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruling has come out of Tehran, and people grow uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get troubled' rearranges the six letters of IRAN and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to order officially or lay down by authority.

clue.text: Prior to musical event duke is upset

indicators.note: the duke and 'is' come before the next piece in the answer

parts.note: a concert is a musical performance

explanation.surface: Just before a recital, a nobleman is in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert someone is to unsettle or fluster them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Wet group of women meeting someone at Westminster

parts.note: the WI, or Women's Institute, is a British organisation for women
an MP, a Member of Parliament, sits at Westminster

explanation.surface: A women's group has a feeble meeting with their local parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI (Women's Institute) is a British community organisation for women; Westminster is the seat of the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a wet is a feeble, ineffectual person, a weakling.

clue.text: Hold back from short break — weather not suitable?

parts.note: a rest is a short pause or break
rain is the sort of weather that spoils outdoor plans

explanation.surface: Someone stays indoors during a brief holiday because the weather is bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to curb or keep in check, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gent healthy, would you say? Maybe not, if he's eaten this

definitions.text: Maybe not, if he's eaten this

indicators.note: the question asks how the words are spoken, pointing to a sound-alike

parts.note: a gentleman is addressed as sir; fit means in good health

explanation.surface: Is the gentleman in good health? Perhaps not, after a huge meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, SIR FIT matches the answer. The definition rides on the first half: a man who has overeaten would not be healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess of food, eaten to overindulgence, would leave a man feeling far from well.

clue.text: Fair women appearing? Old Ben's excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An elderly man named Ben gets worked up when attractive women arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges OLD BENS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Women with fair, light-coloured hair are described by this noun.

clue.text: Get rid of this worker and there may not be any bloomers at home!

definitions.text: Get rid of this worker and there may not be any bloomers at home!

parts.words: Get rid of this worker and there may not be any bloomers at home!
parts.note: bloomers are loaves of bread, so losing the household's earner leaves no bread on the table

explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf; 'bread' is also slang for money, so the person who earns the family income puts loaves in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: The household's main earner brings home the money, slangily the bread, that feeds the family.

clue.text: Rodent responsible for mouldy smell round floating Ark

indicators.note: one piece goes round, or surrounds, the other

parts.note: must is a musty, mouldy smell

indicators.note: floating suggests the letters drift loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A rat is blamed for the musty smell aboard Noah's Ark.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has Noah's vessel afloat; 'floating' is really the signal to rearrange its three letters before 'round' puts the smell around them.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American aquatic animal is a large member of the rodent order.

clue.text: I'm in today, preparing for others to be in tomorrow

definitions.text: I'm in today, preparing for others to be in tomorrow

parts.words: I'm in today, preparing for others to be in tomorrow
parts.note: 'in' means fashionable: this person adopts a style now that everyone else will follow later

explanation.walkthrough: 'In' here means fashionable, not physically present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leads fashion adopts styles before others take them up.

clue.text: Book about one Conservative — see it on the computer?

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large book
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A volume about a Tory politician that can be read on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley or similar symbol is a small image seen in text on a computer screen.

clue.text: Ornament to stay in fixed position, we're told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, so this points to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to freeze is to stop moving and hold still

explanation.surface: A decoration is ordered to remain where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative band along a wall, often carved, is an architectural ornament.

clue.text: Crook is captured — a feature of pantomime?

indicators.note: crook as a verb means to bend, so the letters are bent out of shape

explanation.surface: A villain is caught, as so often happens in a Christmas show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the villain but works as the anagram signal on IS CAPTURED. Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show full of slapstick.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a creamy pie in someone's face is a staple slapstick gag of British pantomime.

clue.text: Lifeless, having lost heart in service

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: dusty means dry and lifeless, dull

explanation.surface: A dull person has lost enthusiasm for working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost heart' takes the central S out of DUSTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a task or service owed, as in being on duty.

clue.text: Familiar with Bill, olde-worlde journalist

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
quaint means charmingly old-fashioned
ED, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone knows a fellow called Bill, an old-fashioned newspaperman.
explanation.definitionFit: Being acquainted with something means having knowledge of it, being familiar with it.

clue.text: A can given a coating of red metal

indicators.note: a coated item is wrapped by the other piece, which goes round it

parts.note: plum is a dark reddish-purple colour
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A tin can is painted red.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silver-white metallic element.

clue.text: Gatecrash and fit in later, having mingled

indicators.note: mingled letters are mixed together into a new order

explanation.surface: A party gatecrasher arrives late and blends in among the guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To infiltrate is to get in secretly, as an uninvited guest slips into a party.

clue.text: Boxer beginning to feel less heavy with pounds shed

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
shed means dropped, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: lighter means weighing less
L is the abbreviation for pounds, from libra

explanation.surface: A boxer starts to feel lighter after losing weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer is a fighter in the ring, one who fights for sport.

clue.text: 'Go away!' we say — with this being thrown?

indicators.note: what we say is spoken, pointing to a word that sounds the same

parts.note: shoo is the cry used to chase someone off

explanation.surface: Someone shouts at an intruder while hurling something at them.
explanation.walkthrough: Throwing footwear at someone is a well-known gesture of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is what gets thrown at someone in insult, the thing hurled in the clue.

clue.text: The man's getting hold of a cover for chemicals

indicators.note: one piece gets hold of the other by enclosing it

parts.note: the man's is the contraction he's
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A man grabs a lid to cover his chemistry set.
explanation.definitionFit: Compounds of a halogen with another element form a class of chemicals.

clue.text: Duck that's cold in stew

indicators.note: the cold letter goes in the other word

parts.note: to souse is to plunge into liquid, to duck
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A duck that is cold is put into a stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Scouse is a meat stew from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a traditional Liverpool meat and vegetable stew.

clue.text: Deny entrance to one appearing without leader

indicators.note: losing the leader means dropping the first letter

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A doorman refuses entry to someone who arrives without their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as being let in, but it is simply a gate; 'without leader' beheads the word one.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to deny or nullify, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Band in church allowed after initial support

indicators.note: the church and allowed pieces come after the opening support piece

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
CE is the Church of England
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A musical band is permitted to play in a church after a first rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band worn round the wrist as jewellery.

clue.text: The woman's right, sir, in Germany

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is correct to address a man politely.
explanation.definitionFit: Herr is the German title equivalent to Mister or sir.

clue.text: Train crack unit here, not hard

indicators.note: crack means break, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An elite unit stationed here is told it is not tough enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' rearranges UNIT HERE and 'not hard' removes H from that pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is the train of attendants following an important person.

clue.text: Place below will do for Rob

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in street names
under means below

explanation.surface: A man named Rob is fine with a seat lower down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a name but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to rob or loot by force.

clue.text: Mere losers battered by society that's cold-hearted

indicators.note: battered letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Society treats mere losers harshly and without pity.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking pity or compassion, a remorseless person is unfeeling, cold-hearted.
